memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then say to Pharaoh, 'This is what the Lord says: Israel is my firstborn son, and I told you, "Let my son go, so that he may worship me." But you refused to let him go; so I will kill your firstborn son.'"" - Exodus 4:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls Israel His firstborn son. It is language of tender ownership — this nation is not merely a people God pities, but a son He loves.

And notice the purpose of the deliverance: let my son go, so that he may worship me. Israel was not being freed simply to be comfortable. They were freed to worship. Freedom from Egypt was freedom for God.

That reframes our own salvation. We were not rescued merely to have better lives. We were rescued to belong to God and worship Him.

Then comes the sobering warning about Pharaoh's firstborn. This is measured justice — a nation that had drowned Hebrew sons is warned of the loss of its own. God gave the warning long in advance, and Pharaoh had every opportunity to relent.

Here is where the gospel takes our breath away. God warned Pharaoh about the death of a son. Then, in the fullness of time, God gave His own Son so that we might live (Jn 3:16). Judgement fell on Him instead of us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I treating my salvation as comfort, or as freedom to worship God?
2. What does it mean to me today that God gave His own firstborn Son?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for calling me Your child and for the Son You gave to save me. Let my freedom be spent in worshipping You. Amen.
